title: Diner-Style American Cheeseburger
changes_from_base: Same patties and pan method as the Classic Cheeseburger. One slice of American cheese per patty goes on after the flip, the sauce becomes a tangy pickle-mayo diner sauce, and the salad is swapped for shredded lettuce, diced white onion and pickles.
summary: A diner-style double cheeseburger with silky melted American cheese and a tangy homemade sauce in every bite.
equipment: large heavy frying pan or cast-iron skillet (at least 26 cm)
lid or large upturned heatproof bowl

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
soft burger buns or brioche-style buns

steps.title: Shape the patties
steps.text: Divide 600g cold beef mince into four 150g portions and shape into patties 11-12cm wide and about 1.5cm thick, slightly wider than the bun to allow for shrinkage. Press a shallow dimple into the centre of each so they stay flat as they cook. Keep the handling light so the mince stays tender.

steps.title: Chill before cooking
steps.text: Chill the patties for 10 minutes before they go anywhere near the pan. This firms the fat so the shape holds and gives a quicker, more even sear once cooking starts.

steps.title: Stir the diner sauce
steps.text: Stir together mayo, ketchup, finely chopped pickles, mustard and paprika in a small bowl, then chill while the patties cook. A short rest in the fridge lets the flavours meld into one tangy, well-rounded sauce.

steps.title: Season just before cooking
steps.text: Season both sides of each patty with salt and pepper right before cooking, not while shaping. Early salting toughens mince into a springy texture rather than a tender one.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Toast the buttered cut sides of the buns in the pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden, then set aside. This protects the bread from turning soggy once the sauce and juicy patty go in.

steps.title: Sear the first side
steps.text: Heat the pan over medium-high for 3 minutes, add 1 teaspoon of oil, then add the patties (2 at a time, or all 4 in a 30cm pan) and leave untouched for 4 minutes. Look for a deep, even brown crust that releases easily from the pan before flipping.

steps.title: Flip and add double cheese
steps.text: Flip each patty once and cook for 3 more minutes, laying a slice of American cheese on top for the final 1-1.5 minutes under a lid. American cheese contains emulsifying salts, so the slice melts into a smooth, even layer rather than breaking apart. The patties are done at 71°C in the centre.

steps.title: Rest briefly
steps.text: Move the patties onto the bun bases and let them rest for 2 minutes. This brief pause keeps the juices in the meat instead of pooling out as soon as you cut in.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread the diner sauce on both cut sides of the bun, then layer shredded lettuce on the bottom, the cheesy patty on top, and finish with diced white onion and pickles. The sauce on both halves means every bite gets that tangy hit, not just the top.

tips: Chill the diner sauce while the patties cook so the flavours have time to meld.
Lay the cheese on as soon as the patty is flipped so it has time to melt into a smooth, even layer over the edges.
Shape the patties gently and press with your fingers only when forming them, never with the spatula once they're in the pan.
Season the mince right before it hits the pan, not while shaping, to keep the texture tender.
storage: Cooked patties keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days, or frozen without buns, sauce or toppings for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly until piping hot and 74°C at the centre before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
